repo.name: tex-fmt
repo.description: An extremely fast LaTeX formatter written in Rust

readme.summary: Exceptionally clear and comprehensive documentation with excellent installation options, usage examples, and configuration details, though troubleshooting content is minimal.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section for common errors or issues users might encounter

injection_risks.description: The `config.parse::<Table>().unwrap_or_else` call can panic if the config file contains invalid TOML, potentially leading to a denial-of-service attack.
The use of `std::process::exit(0)` after generating completions or man pages may lead to unexpected behavior if an attacker can manipulate the input.

critical_findings: Potential denial-of-service attack through invalid TOML config files
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential injection risks and lack of input validation, but no secrets are hardcoded and error exposure is relatively low.

common_complaints: Indentation bugs with special LaTeX syntax (escaped braces, phantoms, unclosed brackets)
Configuration options not working as documented (wrap-chars ignored)
Missing support for LaTeX constructs (tables, minted environments, directlua blocks)
Platform/distribution support gaps (Ubuntu packages, texlive CTAN)
Line wrapping limitations and bugs (verb commands, bibliography items)
praise_themes: Performance and speed compared to alternatives like latexindent
sentiment.summary: Active community engagement with bug reports, but slow maintainer response and accumulation of unresolved core functionality issues suggest declining project health and potential maintenance burden.
